title: Annotatio IV §.XVIII: Wycliffe vs Consubstantiation / Impanation — impossible and heretical
pass_a_gloss: But CONSUBSTANTIATION he refutes by these: I am certain, he says, that the sentence of Impanation is impossible and heretical, because thus Christ’s body would be made not only by the celebrating Presbyter but also by the baker; and generally the celebrating Priest would break Christ’s neck and all His members.
pass_b_english: Against Consubstantiation / Impanation Wycliffe is certain: the sentence is impossible and heretical.
Otherwise Christ’s body would be made not only by the celebrating priest but by the baker — and the celebrant would break Christ’s neck and all His members.
source_text: CONSUBSTANTIATIONEM autem hisce refutat: Sum certus, inquit, quod sententia Impanationis est impossibilis atque hæreticæ, quia sic corpus Christi nedum foret factum à Presbytero celebrante, sed & à pistore; & generaliter Sacerdos celebrans, collum & omnia membra Christi frangeret.
